sources.entry: OpenSlides - Presentation and assembly system for managing and projecting agenda, motions and elections of an assembly. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: OpenSlides is a free, web-based presentation and assembly system for managing and projecting the agenda, motions and elections of an assembly.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OpenSlides as a free, web-based system for managing and projecting agenda, motions and elections for an assembly. It points to external docs for installation and for more information, so the README itself contains no feature list. It names a separate install guide for OpenSlides 4 and a development readme for contributors. The README notes that updating to OpenSlides 4.3.0 introduces breaking changes and links to an upgrade info document. The project is distributed under the MIT License.
use_cases: running an assembly with agenda management
projecting agenda items during a presentation
how_to_run: Follow the OpenSlides 4 install instructions linked from the README
Read the 4.3.0 upgrade info document before updating to 4.3.0 or later
See the development readme for developer setup
notable: Web-based presentation and assembly system for agendas, motions and elections
Free/Libre Open Source software under the MIT License
Docker listed as a deployment option in the awesome-selfhosted entry
Has a separate development readme for contributors
caveats: Updating to OpenSlides 4.3.0 introduces breaking changes
The README gives no detailed feature list or system requirements; these are in external documents
